title: Man shot by police in Oakville, Ont., had recently moved from B.C.
article: An armed man killed in a confrontation with police in this community west of Toronto had recently returned to Ontario from B.C. after losing or leaving his job.
Steve Remian, 38, died after being shot several times by three officers, two of them tactical unit members, early Saturday in a park in the town's posh east end.
Reports said one of those bullets is believed to have hit Remian in the head.
Remian had moved to B.C. to work and recently returned to Oakville, where he lived in the past and has family. RCMP in B.C. were trying to dig up background on the man, Bliss said.
Four officers were initially designated as subject officers, meaning that they had shot at Remian, but evidence suggests there were three officers, Bliss said.
Their actions are now under scrutiny by the SIU, a civilian agency that investigates incidents involving police and civilians which have resulted in serious injury or death.
Police began looking for Remian and his car after receiving a call from a person at a Tim Hortons about an hour before the shooting.
Bliss said the man was reported to be acting strangely and threatened to harm himself and others.
The caller had also seen a rifle.
By the time officers arrived at the coffee shop Remian had left, but another patrolling cruiser spotted his car a short time later.
With flashing lights, police followed the car into the park, where the man drove until he got wedged in bush and woods.
Remian apparently made no effort to lose police during the short drive from when he was spotted and when he was cornered in the park.
Despite numerous pleas to drop the rifle, Remian apparently lifted the firearm and police opened fire.
Bliss said it was not known late Sunday if Remian opened fire at police.
